fix_commit.message: Bug 1954042 - Check OOM condition after readAllocSiteIndex(). r=rhunt
fix_commit.author: Yury Delendik

findings.title: Missing OOM Check After Vector Append Leads to Out-of-Bounds Access
findings.message: The `readAllocSiteIndex()` function appends to a vector using `masm.append(wasm::AllocSitePatch())` but does not check if the append operation succeeded. When an OOM condition occurs during `masm.append()`, the vector does not grow, but the function still returns the pre-append length as the index. Subsequently, `loadAllocSiteInstanceData()` uses this index to access `masm.allocSitesPatches()[allocSiteIndex]`, which will be out of bounds because the vector did not actually grow. This results in an out-of-bounds write when `setPatchOffset()` is called on the non-existent element.
findings.suggestion: The function should return a boolean to indicate success/failure and use an out parameter for the index. The OOM condition from masm.append() must be checked before returning the index. All callers must check the return value and handle the OOM case by returning false to propagate the error up the call stack.

ground_truth.root_cause: The `readAllocSiteIndex()` function captures the vector length before appending a new element, then returns this length as the index for the newly appended element. However, if the `masm.append()` call fails due to OOM, the vector does not grow, making the returned index invalid (pointing one past the actual end of the vector). The subsequent use of this index in `loadAllocSiteInstanceData()` results in accessing memory beyond the vector's bounds.
